campaign: ISL Recognition Pipeline Stabilization — Phase 1 paired browser Canvas validation

methodology.browser_canvas: Actual Chrome/Edge HTMLVideoElement -> Canvas 640px width -> toDataURL(image/jpeg,0.92) bytes; no OpenCV resize/re-encode in this path.
methodology.opencv_native_reference: OpenCV-decoded native source video frames matched to browser video.currentTime timestamps using source FPS; encoded to lossless PNG only for the existing MediaPipe JPEG-byte decode API. This is a native-resolution reference path, not a browser decoder parity claim.
methodology.frame_alignment: Frame indices are compared at the same browser-recorded timestamps; OpenCV source frame selection uses round(timestamp*source_fps). Failed extraction slots are excluded from per-coordinate differences; each model sequence uses successful extracted frames in temporal order, matching the app's successful-frame sequence behavior.
limitations: The browser capture page reproduces the production Canvas resize/JPEG settings but runs from local validation video files rather than the live webcam.
The local batch receiver removes WebSocket bufferedAmount/network-pressure drops from this diagnostic; timer duplicate skips and browser decoder dropped-frame counters are still recorded separately.
The OpenCV native reference uses OpenCV's decoder and FPS-based nearest-frame selection; it is not byte-identical to Chrome's internal decoded source frame.
The active modern MediaPipe Pose adapter uses full Pose indices 0..24 and is not proven coordinate-equivalent to historical upper_body_only=True.
This benchmark assesses paired pipeline behavior on the validation split; it does not establish external-signer generalisation or production readiness.
